questions.question: D1 — Convert the Save button visual hierarchy gap into an implementation task? <gstack-qid:plan-design-review-ia-1>

options.label: A) Add as implementation task (Recommended)
options.description: Convert the gap into a concrete task: 'Apply filled primary styling (#1d4ed8, white text) to Save; ghost styling to Reset, Cancel, Export per DESIGN.md.' Completeness: 10/10 — implementer has a specific, verifiable task with exact tokens.

options.label: B) Add token reference only
options.description: Add a note in the gap section pointing to the DESIGN.md spec, but don't create a formal task. Completeness: 7/10 — the fix is findable but not surfaced for sprint planning or checklist use.

options.label: C) Leave as described gap
options.description: Keep the gap as prose only. Completeness: 3/10 — the problem is named but implementers must cross-reference DESIGN.md to find the fix, risking it being missed or done wrong.

questions.question: D2 — Add the pending-save state spec as an implementation task? <gstack-qid:plan-design-review-states-1>

options.label: A) Add as implementation task (Recommended)
options.description: Task: 'Render an inline spinner beside the text “Saving…” inside the disabled Save button; set aria-busy=true on the button; under prefers-reduced-motion, remove the spinner but preserve disabled state and text.' Completeness: 10/10 — implementer has the full DESIGN.md spec with the a11y attribute and the motion variant.

options.label: B) Add note in Motion gap only
options.description: Reference the DESIGN.md spinner pattern in the Motion gap section without a formal task. Completeness: 7/10 — the fix is documented but not actionable as a discrete work item.

options.label: C) Leave Motion gap as-is
options.description: Keep the gap description as a known issue without specifying the fix. Completeness: 3/10 — ships a frozen page during 2-5s saves; users may try clicking Save again (duplicate submit).

questions.question: D3 — Add a state coverage table to the plan body for implementer reference? <gstack-qid:plan-design-review-states-2>

options.label: A) Add state table (Recommended)
options.description: Insert a feature × state table (Form load / Save / Export / Dirty state × Loading / Empty / Error / Success / Pending). No new design decisions — all cells derive from existing specs. Completeness: 10/10 — implementers can verify each state against a single reference.

options.label: B) Leave states in prose only
options.description: Keep the existing prose descriptions without a structured table. Completeness: 7/10 — specs are all there but scattered across paragraphs; edge cases like Export error during dirty-edit are harder to spot.

questions.question: D4 — Add a user journey storyboard to the plan? <gstack-qid:plan-design-review-journey-1>

options.label: A) Add storyboard (Recommended)
options.description: Render the accepted journey as a step/user-does/user-feels/plan-specifies table (8 rows covering happy path, save failure, cancel with dirty state, first-time new account). No new design decisions — pure rendering of existing specs. Completeness: 10/10 — implementers understand the emotional arc and can verify the spec covers each moment.

options.label: B) Keep one-sentence journey description
options.description: Leave the current one-sentence happy-path description. Completeness: 5/10 — the journey exists but reads like a state machine; error recovery arcs and first-time experience aren't visible without cross-referencing multiple paragraphs.

questions.question: D5 — Convert the spacing gap into an implementation task with explicit DESIGN.md scale? <gstack-qid:plan-design-review-ds-2>

options.label: A) Add as implementation task (Recommended)
options.description: Task: 'Apply the 8px spacing scale: between-section gaps 32px, between-field-group gaps 24px, label-to-input gaps 8px. Remove any 16px gap — no context in DESIGN.md uses 16px here.' Completeness: 10/10 — implementer has exact values and knows which to remove.

options.label: B) Reference DESIGN.md scale without a task
options.description: Add a note pointing to the 8px base system in DESIGN.md. Completeness: 7/10 — the scale is accessible but the erroneous 16px value isn't explicitly called out for removal, risking it staying in the implementation.

options.label: C) Leave as gap description
options.description: Keep the spacing gap as a prose description only. Completeness: 3/10 — ships inconsistent vertical rhythm; the UI will have a subtle broken-grid feel that erodes trust without an obvious cause.

questions.question: D6 — Convert the error color gap into an implementation task with WCAG-compliant tokens? <gstack-qid:plan-design-review-ds-3>

options.label: A) Add as implementation task (Recommended)
options.description: Task: 'Apply error.text #991b1b on error.surface #fef2f2, plus an error icon and explicit text label. Measured contrast 5.9:1 — passes WCAG AA (4.5:1 required for normal text).' Completeness: 10/10 — implementer has exact hex values, knows the icon requirement, and can verify with a contrast checker.

options.label: B) Note the DESIGN.md tokens only
options.description: Add a note pointing to the DESIGN.md error color pair without a formal task. Completeness: 7/10 — the fix is findable but ships as a follow-up item rather than a merge requirement.

options.label: C) Leave as gap description
options.description: Keep the ~3:1 contrast gap as prose only. Completeness: 3/10 — ships a WCAG AA violation; users with low vision miss error messages; legal and audit risk.

questions.question: D7 — Convert the typography gap into an implementation task with the two-role system? <gstack-qid:plan-design-review-ds-4>

options.label: A) Add as implementation task (Recommended)
options.description: Task: 'Apply two font-size roles: 16px for body text, form labels, and helper text; 20px for the h2 section headings (Profile, Notifications). Remove 14px (below universal-rule minimum) and 18px (no role in the design system).' Completeness: 10/10 — implementer has both the target values and the values to remove, with the WCAG rationale for the 14px removal.

options.label: B) Reference two-role system only
options.description: Add a note pointing to the DESIGN.md two-role spec without listing which sizes to remove. Completeness: 7/10 — the target is clear but 14px and 18px may linger without an explicit removal instruction.

options.label: C) Leave as gap description
options.description: Keep the 3-size description as a known gap. Completeness: 3/10 — ships 14px text that violates the universal-rule body minimum; flat hierarchy where headings don't distinguish themselves from body.

questions.question: D8 — Address the skip navigation link gap? <gstack-qid:plan-design-review-a11y-1>

options.label: A) Add verification task: confirm skip link exists in app shell (Recommended)
options.description: Task: 'Verify that the persistent app navigation includes a skip-to-main-content link (WCAG 2.1 SC 2.4.1 Bypass Blocks). If absent, add Skip to content before the nav.' Completeness: 10/10 — WCAG 2.4.1 compliance confirmed or addressed; keyboard users can bypass nav on every page load.

options.label: B) Note it as a known gap, defer to app shell audit
options.description: Add a note that skip nav is out of this form's scope and should be verified at app shell level. Completeness: 7/10 — the question is raised but the settings page may ship with a WCAG 2.4.1 gap if the shell audit doesn't happen alongside this PR.

options.label: C) Out of scope — leave unaddressed
options.description: The plan covers only the settings form; skip nav is a shell concern. No action. Completeness: 5/10 — risk: if no skip link exists, keyboard users must tab through all nav items on every form interaction cycle.

answers.D8 \u2014 Address the skip navigation li: A) Add verification task: confirm skip link exists in app shell (Recommended)
